title: Tanganyika
capsule: Tanganyika gained independence from British trusteeship on 9 December 1961, becoming the first territory in British East Africa to do so, and became a republic on 9 December 1962 under President Julius Nyerere. As the mainland successor to the former German East Africa and subsequent League of Nations mandate, it entered independence with a largely agrarian economy dependent on sisal, coffee, and cotton, and a small bureaucratic class. Nyerere's TANU party pursued African socialism and maintained pan-Africanist commitments, including sheltering ANC and liberation-movement offices. On 26 April 1964, following a revolution that overthrew the Sultanate of Zanzibar, Tanganyika merged with Zanzibar to form the United Republic of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, renamed Tanzania later that year.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial boundaries are precisely defined by the former mandate border and are well attested; the from date of 1961 aligns with independence and the to date of 1965 (the batch gives 1965, slightly after the 1964 union) reflects the period of constitutional transition.
